items.title: John Joseph Interview, 1962-01-18
items.q: Only three men. Davy Jones, Floyd Jackson, Henry Sawyer. Only three men living in the band.

ctx.x: And Davy Jones you say was there and he's still alive too? Oh yeah he's living.
Only three men. Davy Jones, Floyd Jackson, Henry Sawyer. Only three men living in the band. And Dennis Harris.
The clarinet. The clarinet. And who are the two cornet players?

items.title: John Joseph Interview, 1962-01-18
items.q: Best man. Best man I've seen.

ctx.x: And Henry Sawyer played slide and trombone. Slide and trombone. When did he take up the slide and trombone?
Years ago. Everybody was playing those barit trombone. The barit trombone. So he was the first one you saw. Best man. Best man I've seen.
How long did Jones stay on snare drum?

items.title: John Joseph Interview, 1962-01-18
items.q: First man I've seen with a slide.

ctx.x: Drummer. And so Henry Sawyer was playing a slide. You can see in the picture he's playing a slide.
Drummer. First man. First man I've seen with a slide. And I know I'm old. First man I've seen with a slide.
How old are you? About seventeen or what?

items.title: John Joseph Interview, 1958-11-26
items.q: David Jones, Floyd Jackson, Henry Sawyer. ... They came down here in those time and outplayed all of the band down here.

ctx.x: Now the trombone player, you're saying he played slide, huh?
Slide, that's one of the first slides I've ever seen. I've been here for years. He brought a slide here when he didn't have any here in yours. Henry Sawyer.
Henry Sawyer. That's right. See, how many players are there? One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight pieces.
